title: Optimization and constrained extrema
terms: optimization; max/min problem; local extremum; absolute extremum; endpoint test; constraint reduction.

exposition.text:
A local extremum compares nearby domain points, whereas an absolute extremum compares
the entire domain. At an interior local extremum where the derivative exists, it must vanish.
On a closed bounded interval, a continuous function attains extrema, so compare values at all
interior critical points and both endpoints. A zero derivative is a candidate, not a conclusion.
Translate a word problem into an objective function and its actual feasible domain. Eliminate
one variable using the constraint, differentiate, and check that the candidate is admissible. On
open or unbounded domains, also investigate limiting behavior at excluded boundaries; a supre-
mum may not be attained. A second-derivative test gives local classification but does not alone
establish global optimality.

question.text:

For nonnegative x, y with x + 2y = 12, what is the maximum of x y?
(A) 64 (B) 96 (C) 128 (D) 192 (E) 256

solution.text:
2 3
Substitute y = (12 − x)/2 on 0 ≤ x ≤ 12. The objective is 6x − x /2, with derivative
2
12x − 3x /2 = (3x/2)(8 − x). The positive interior maximizer is x = 8, y = 2, giving 128;
endpoints give zero.

For a, b > 0, what is the maximum of x (1 − x) on [0, 1]?
a b a+b a+b a b a a b b
(A) a b /(a + b) (B) (a + b) /(a b ) (C) a /(a + b) (D) b /(a + b) (E) 1

solution.text:
On (0, 1) logarithmic differentiation gives derivative sign equal to that of a/x − b/(1 − x). It
changes from positive to negative at x = a/(a + b). Substitution yields the displayed value,
and both endpoint values are zero.

question.text:
3
At which points does f (x) = x − 3x attain its absolute minimum on [−2, 3/2]?
(A) x = −2 only (B) x = −1 only
(C) x = 1 only (D) x = −2 and x = 1
(E) x = −1 and x = 3/2

solution.text:
The interior critical points are −1 and 1. Compare all four candidates: f(−2) = −2,
f(−1) = 2, f (1) = −2, and f(3/2) = −9/8. The same global minimum occurs at an
endpoint and an interior stationary point; a local classification alone misses the tie.
